ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of an ideal transformer is n1∶n2＝10∶1. The primary coil input sinusoidal alternating voltage is as shown in the figure, and the secondary coil is connected to a resistor with resistance 22 Ω. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Multi-Physics open-ended question 1
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of an ideal transformer is n1∶n2=10∶1. The primary coil input sinusoidal alternating voltage is as shown in the figure, and the secondary coil is connected to a resistor with resistance 22 Ω. How many times per second does the direction of the alternating current in the resistor change?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of an ideal transformer is n1∶n2=10∶1. The primary coil input sinusoidal alternating voltage is as shown in the figure, and the secondary coil is connected to a resistor with resistance 22 Ω. How many times per second does the direction of the alternating current in the resistor change?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled u/V, indicating the primary coil input voltage; the horizontal axis is labeled t/×10^-2 s. The waveform is sinusoidal alternating current, and the maximum value and minimum value are labeled 220√2 V and -220√2 V respectively. The waveform starts from t=0 crossing zero, crosses zero again at about t=1×10^-2 s, and returns again to the same-phase zero-crossing position at t=2×10^-2 s, so one period T=2×10^-2 s can be read. Reasoning: The frequency of the primary coil input voltage is f=1/T=1/(2×10^-2 s)=50 Hz. An ideal transformer only changes the magnitudes of voltage and current and does not change the frequency of the alternating current, so the frequency of the alternating current in the 22 Ω resistor connected to the secondary coil is still 50 Hz. A sinusoidal alternating current changes direction 2 times in each period, so the number of direction changes per second is 2f=2×50=100 times.
